# Shehbaz Sharif, Pakistan, 2024: 2B.3 evidence note

Bounded search completed with multiple query formulations. Best read: **mostly favorable**, but with a real mixed record. Sharif’s 2024 public posture often distinguished defense, diplomacy, and nuclear-safety institutions from escalation, but he also used nationalist / coercive rhetoric on Kashmir and operated in a rights-constrained political environment.

| Polarity | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Favorable | Peace in South Asia depends on settlement of Kashmir dispute: PM | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-21 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/21-09-2024/peace-in-south-asia-depends-on-settlement-of-kashmir-dispute-pm | Sharif said Pakistan strongly believes in peace and stability through dialogue, and that lasting regional peace depends on a peaceful settlement of Kashmir. This is direct evidence that he framed security in terms of actual diplomacy rather than prestige or manufactured threats. | 2B.3; also 2B.1, 1B.8 |
| Favorable | PM urges UN to take action against Israel’s genocidal acts | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-26 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/26-09-2024/pm-urges-un-to-take-action-against-israels-genocidal-acts | In his UNGA speech, Sharif urged confidence-building measures to prevent war between major powers and to ease rising tensions. That is explicit de-escalation language, consistent with separating genuine security needs from nationalist escalation. | 2B.3; also 2B.1, 1B.8 |
| Favorable | Pakistan’s nuclear-security regime page | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan | May 2024 update; standing page | https://www.mofa.gov.pk/vienna-pakistans-nuclear-safety-seccurity-regime | The government says Pakistan updated its Nuclear Security Regime booklet in May 2024, renewed practical arrangements with the IAEA, and keeps NCA/SPD oversight formalized. This points to precaution, transparency, and institutionalized security rather than threat inflation or personalist prestige politics. | 2B.3; also 1B.3, 1B.7, 1B.9 |
| Favorable | Arms Control And Disarmament | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan | Standing page; current version cites May 2024 update | https://mofa.gov.pk/arms-control-and-disarmament | Pakistan’s policy page says it supports CTBT objectives, a unilateral testing moratorium, FMCT negotiations, IAEA safeguards, reciprocal inspections proposals, UNSCR 1540 implementation, export controls, and multilateral nonproliferation norms. This is the clearest institutional evidence of distinguishing real security needs from prestige or manufactured threat narratives. | 2B.3; also 1B.4, 1B.6, 1B.9 |
| Mixed / negative | PM stresses for peaceful solution of global challenges | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-27 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/27-09-2024/pm-urges-india-to-engage-in-dialogue-for-resolution-of-jk-dispute | Sharif urged India into dialogue for Kashmir, but the same speech also warned Pakistan would “respond most decisively” to Indian aggression and described India’s war doctrine in nuclearized terms. This is the main counterexample: defensive framing was present, but so was nationalist brinkmanship that can serve leverage or domestic rallying. | 2B.3; also 1B.1, 1B.2, 1B.8, 1B.10 |
| Mixed / negative-adjacent | Pakistan election-day internet shutdown is a reckless attack on people’s rights | Amnesty International | 2024-02-08 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/pakistan-election-day-internet-shutdown-is-a-reckless-attack-on-peoples-rights/ | Amnesty condemned the election-day telecom and mobile internet shutdown as a rights violation. This does not prove nuclear-risk manipulation, but it does show a coercive political environment around Sharif’s ascent, which weakens a clean reading that all security behavior was purely defensive. | 2B.3; also 1B.8, 1B.10 |

## Synthesis

- Best-supported conclusion: Sharif **often did distinguish** genuine security needs from escalation, especially in his dialogue-first Kashmir and multilateral nuclear-safety messaging.
- The strongest contrary evidence is **rhetorical nationalism and brinkmanship** around India/Kashmir, not a documented campaign of invented threats.
- I did **not** find reliable 2024 evidence that he clearly used nuclear/security policy for revenge, prestige, or a deliberate diversionary war.
- Confidence should stay **moderate**, because the record is mostly public rhetoric plus institutional policy, not internal decision memos.
